front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《5》

en: Meeting you
In the most beautiful season
The music, splendid as wine, as the moon
Life, like the morning dew
A single drop
Left for the flower-dew wine

points.zh:
君不見
黄河之水天上來，奔流到海不復回。
君不見
高堂明鏡悲白髮，朝如青絲暮成雪。
人生得意須盡歡，莫使金樽空對月。
天生我材必有用，千金散盡還復來。
烹羊宰牛且爲樂，會須一飲三百杯。
岑夫子，丹丘生，將進酒，杯莫停。
但願長醉不復醒。
古來聖賢皆寂寞，惟有飲者留其名。
--唐。李白《 將進酒 》
points.en:
You don't see —
The Yellow River's waters come down from the sky, rushing to the sea and never returning.
You don't see —
In tall halls, sad mirrors reflect white hair, black as silk at dawn turned to snow by evening.
When life goes well, one should revel fully; do not let the golden cup face the moon empty.
Heaven gave me talent for a reason; a thousand pieces of gold, once spent, will come again.
Boil the lamb, slaughter the ox, let us make merry; when we drink, we should drink three hundred cups at once.
Master Cen, and Scholar Danqiu, bring in the wine — do not let the cups stop.
I wish only to remain long drunk and never wake.
Since ancient times, sages and worthies have all been forgotten; only those who drank left their names behind.
-- Tang Dynasty. Li Bai, "Bring in the Wine" (將進酒)

en: Watching the lake water before the cluster of peaks
Listening to the echo within the echo
The reflection is utterly still

zh: 下雨的街頭，你對自己說
en: On the rainy street, you say to yourself
Let me be a single leaf!
Autumn wind dyes it red, carried off with the stream----
Sitting a while in a loft in Lukang
A pot of tea
Blowing out three hundred years of hardship

points.zh: 一府二鹿三艋舺，是一句台灣諺語，描叙清朝時期全島三大港市的盛況。一府是台南府，二鹿是彰化鹿港鎮，三艋舺是台北艋舺 (今萬華 )。此諺語反應台灣由南至北的開墾史，以及各地域仰賴海洋貿易的情況。鹿港可能因當時鹿麋成群，輸出鹿角，鹿皮，鹿脯而得名。 鹿港的興起，係掌握諸多地理地形優勢。鹿港爲河港城市，可直接出入台灣海峽，由鹿港到大陸閩粵的海域航程，是台灣諸海港中距離最短。當時濁水溪主流由鹿港出海，船隻可上溯航行，連接中部各地。1785年至1845年是鹿港的全盛時期。其後，鹿港的港口優勢因泥沙淤積而逐漸沒落，千帆雲集風光不再。嘉慶中葉後，來往商船由南部王功港取代。道光年間，王功港步入淤塞後塵。
points.en: "First Fu, second Lu, third Mengjia" is a Taiwanese proverb describing the prosperity of the island's three great port cities during the Qing dynasty. "Fu" refers to Tainan Prefecture, "Lu" refers to Lukang Township in Changhua, and "Mengjia" refers to Mengjia in Taipei (present-day Wanhua). The proverb reflects the history of Taiwan's development from south to north, and the reliance of each region on maritime trade. Lukang ("deer port") may have gotten its name because herds of deer gathered there at the time, and deer antlers, hides, and dried venison were exported from the port. Lukang's rise was due to a number of geographic advantages. As a river port city, it had direct access to the Taiwan Strait, and the sea voyage from Lukang to the Fujian-Guangdong coast of mainland China was the shortest among all of Taiwan's ports. At the time, the main channel of the Zhuoshui River flowed out to sea at Lukang, allowing ships to travel upstream and connect with various parts of central Taiwan. The period from 1785 to 1845 was Lukang's golden age. Afterward, Lukang's advantages as a port gradually declined due to silt accumulation, and the once-crowded harbor of a thousand sails lost its former glory. After the middle years of the Jiaqing era, merchant ships shifted to Wanggong Port in the south. During the Daoguang era, Wanggong Port in turn began to silt up.

en: When memory turns into song
Then there is a place
We can go back together
Dusk gradually falling
Just how many journeys must accumulate
Only then can one sit and watch life like drifting clouds

points.zh:
中歲頗好道，晚家南山陲
興來每獨往，勝事空自知
行到水窮處，坐看雲起時
偶然值林叟，談笑無還期
--唐。王維《 終南別業》
points.en:
In my middle years I came to love the Way; in old age I made my home at the foot of Zhongnan Mountain.
When the mood strikes, I go off alone; the finest moments are known only to myself.
I walk until the water runs out, then sit and watch the clouds rise.
By chance I meet an old man of the forest; we talk and laugh, with no thought of when to return.
-- Wang Wei (Tang dynasty), "My Retreat at Mount Zhongnan"

en: Late spring, a light rain
Grass's color like light smoke, beneath the flowering tree
I want to stand here a while longer
Some memories are a pale, shallow blue
Life's waystation
Wandering a few times

zh: 《長日將盡》，我披塵沾露千里歸來
en: "The Remains of the Day" -- cloaked in dust and dew, I return from a thousand miles
Please, 'Never Let Me Go,' do not forget
This moment, what you feel for me in your heart

points.zh:
石黒一雄 ( Kazuo Ishiguro )，日裔英籍小說家，2017諾貝爾文學獎得主。瑞典文學院授獎評論詞 : 「在我們與世界融爲一体的幻覺下，他在感情力量巨大的小說中，爲我們揭示了一道深淵 」。其代表作品有：
1986年：《浮世畫家》（An Artist of the Floating World）
1989年：《長日將盡》（The Remains of the Day）
2000年：《我輩孤雛》（When We Were Orphans）
2005年 :  《別譲我走》 ( Never Let Me Go )
2010年：《夜曲：音樂與黄昏五故事》（Nocturnes: Five Stories of Music and Nightfall）
2015年：《被掩埋的巨人》（The Buried Giant ）
《長日將盡》獲得英國1989年布克獎 : 「以哀而不傷的筆觸，平實卻又奇崛，把世界帶到讀者面前……正如一首夜曲，又不止是一首夜曲。」
《別讓我走》美國時代周刊評爲2005年十大最佳小說和1923至2005年間百部優秀英語小說:「女孩緊緊閉上雙眼，雙手擁抱著過去那個友善的世界，一個她內心明白已經不再存在的地方，但她還是緊抓著不放，懇求它別放開她的手……。」
points.en:
Kazuo Ishiguro, a Japanese-born British novelist, winner of the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature. In the Swedish Academy's citation: "in novels of great emotional force, he has uncovered the abyss beneath our illusory sense of connection with the world." His representative works include:
1986: 'An Artist of the Floating World'
1989: 'The Remains of the Day'
2000: 'When We Were Orphans'
2005: 'Never Let Me Go'
2010: 'Nocturnes: Five Stories of Music and Nightfall'
2015: 'The Buried Giant'
'The Remains of the Day' won Britain's 1989 Booker Prize: "with a restrained yet vivid touch, at once plain and extraordinary, it brings the world before the reader... truly a nocturne, and yet more than just a nocturne."
'Never Let Me Go' was named by Time magazine one of the ten best novels of 2005 and one of the hundred best English-language novels from 1923 to 2005: "The girl shuts her eyes tightly, her arms embracing that once-friendly world of the past, a place she knows in her heart no longer exists, yet still she clings to it, begging it not to let go of her hand...."
